bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42521498 (glog): Dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_demangle [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42521498
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source in gt_results/arvo_42521498/_work/src/glog / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 4-byte string `0x5f 0x5a 0x6e 0x39` (`"_Zn9"`). `ParseMangledName()` accepts the `_Z` prefix and leaves the suffix `n9` for `ParseSourceName()`. In `ParseNumber()`, the leading `n` is parsed as a negative-sign marker and the digit `9` is accumulated, so `ParseSourceName()` receives `length == -9` with `state->mangled_cur` already advanced to the NUL terminator that the harness appended after the 4-byte input. Vulnerable `ParseIdentifier()` only rejects `length == -1` or a positive length that exceeds the remaining input; with `length == -9`, `AtLeastNumCharsRemaining(..., -9)` vacuously returns true because its loop never executes for a negative bound. The function therefore falls through to `state->mangled_cur += length`, rewinding the parse cursor from the terminator to five bytes before the start of the stack buffer. `ParseUnqualifiedName()` then evaluates `Optional(ParseAbiTags(state))` after the successful `ParseSourceName(state)` call, and the first `ParseAbiTag()` probes the out-of-bounds cursor in `ParseOneCharToken(state, 'B')`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow read at `src/demangle.cc:211`. The patch's relevant fix hunk adds a `length < 0 || ... > StrLen(...)` rejection before the pointer rewind; the separate `Append()` null-output guard is not needed for this witness.

source.description: Source. When `ParseSourceName()` parses the witness suffix `n9`, this branch consumes the attacker-controlled `n` and creates the negative-sign state that later makes the identifier length negative.
source.value_from: The exact staged PoC `gt_results/arvo_42521498/poc` is the 4-byte string `0x5f 0x5a 0x6e 0x39` (`"_Zn9"`). After `ParseMangledName()` accepts the `_Z` prefix at `src/demangle.cc:484`, `ParseEncoding()` reaches `ParseSourceName()` with `state->mangled_cur` on `"n9"`, and this branch consumes the `n` byte as the sign marker for the upcoming length.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `ParseIdentifier()` only rejects `length == -1` or a positive length that exceeds the remaining string. With the witness, `length == -9`; `AtLeastNumCharsRemaining(..., -9)` returns true because its loop never executes for a negative bound, so the function accepts a negative identifier length instead of rejecting it.
root_cause.note: The fix hunk adds `if (length < 0 || static_cast<std::size_t>(length) > StrLen(state->mangled_cur)) return false;` before the later `state->mangled_cur += length` pointer update. The separate `Append()` null-output hardening hunk in `patch.diff` is not required for this saved ASan crash.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `ParseAbiTag()` probes the optionally-following abi-tag prefix by reading `state->mangled_cur[0]`, but the earlier negative-length rewind has already moved that cursor before the fuzz buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan report is `dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/demangle.cc:211:7` with stack `ParseOneCharToken -> ParseAbiTag -> OneOrMore -> ParseAbiTags -> ParseUnqualifiedName -> ParseUnscopedName -> ParseUnscopedTemplateName -> ParseName -> ParseEncoding -> ParseMangledName -> ParseTopLevelMangledName -> Demangle`.

fine_trace.note: Source. While parsing the witness suffix `n9`, `ParseNumber()` consumes the leading `n`, sets `sign = -1`, and leaves `state->mangled_cur` on the digit `9`.
The digit loop reads the remaining `9`, updates `number` to 9, and advances `p` to the NUL terminator that the harness appended after the 4-byte input.
`ParseNumber()` commits `state->mangled_cur` at the terminator and stores `length = -9` for `ParseSourceName()`. This is the concrete tainted length later consumed by `ParseIdentifier()`.

With `length = -9`, `length == -1` is false and `AtLeastNumCharsRemaining(..., -9)` returns true because `for (ssize_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)` executes zero iterations for a negative `n`. The malformed negative identifier length is therefore accepted instead of rejected.

Using `length = -9` rewinds the cursor from the `Buffer[4]` terminator to five bytes before `Buffer[0]`, so the parser state now points outside the fuzz buffer and into the left alloca redzone that ASan later reports.

Because `ParseSourceName(state)` returned true with the out-of-bounds cursor from step 5, this alternative immediately evaluates `Optional(ParseAbiTags(state))`. `Optional()` always returns true, but its argument is still evaluated first, so abi-tag parsing begins on the invalid cursor instead of stopping here.

Sink. `ParseAbiTags()` immediately calls `OneOrMore(ParseAbiTag, state)`, and `ParseAbiTag()` starts with `ParseOneCharToken(state, 'B')`. This dereference is therefore the first out-of-bounds read from the rewound cursor.

format.contract: An exact 4-byte input: `0x5f 0x5a 0x6e 0x39` (`"_Zn9"`). The harness copies those 4 bytes into `Buffer`, appends a NUL terminator, and passes the resulting string to `google::Demangle()`. This precise witness yields the negative source-name length `-9` described above.
